To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a common fragment ion, the fluorenylium ion (C13H9+) (m/z = 165) formed during the fragmentation of three different PAH species (C13H11, C14H12, and C14H12) using infrared multiple-photon ion spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations.

the m/z =165 ion formed from the electron ionization of the three-ring PAHs, fluorene, 9,10-DHP, and 9, 10-DHA, has a similar infrared spectrum, and is assigned as fluorenyl, C13H9+, based on theoretical calculations.

the m/z 165 fragment of three different three-ringed polycyclic aromatic compounds, fluorene (9H-fluorene), 9, 10-dihydro-9, 10-anthracenecarbaldehyde (9, 10-DHA), and 9-phenanthrenol (9-PN), is a fluorenyl radical cation, which is a common product in electron ionization-induced fragmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and structural characterization of a common fragment product of three-ring PAHs.
the identification of the product ions formed from the electron-ionization of three-ring PAHs and the elucidation of their fragmentation pathways.
elucidating the chemical composition of the interstellar medium (ISM) and the chemistry of PAHs and their role in interstellar space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluorenylium ion is the most common product formed during the fragmentation of PAHs with three rings.

the fluorenylium ion, a closed-shell ion with a singlet electronic state, is a common product of the fragmentation of three different PAH species, fluorene, 9,10- dihydrophenanthrene, and 9, 10-dihydro anthracene.
fluorene, dihydrophenanthrene, and dihydroanthracene are all converted to the fluorene cation upon electron ionization, which is a common fragmentation product for PAHs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fluorenylium cation is a common fragment of the electron-impact ionization of three-ring PAHs and can serve as a marker for these PAHs.

we have identified a single fragmentation product (the closed shell fluorenyl radical cation) of three different three ring PAHs and have proposed a decomposition pathway for each of the three precursors to the product.

we have found a common fragment ion in the electron ionization-induced fragmentation of fluorene, 9,10-DHP, and 9, 10-DHA, and that the fragment has been identified as the fluorenylium ion by infrared spectroscopy and theoretical calculation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single isomer, C13H9+, can be formed from three different three-ring precursors.
the fragmentation products of gaseous PAHs are not random and that a common fragment is produced during fragmentation of three-ring PAHs.
the fluorenylium ion is a common fragmentation product of PAHs and that this ion can be used to probe the fragmentation pathways of PAH molecules.
